For a Hilbert pair $(E_0,E_1)$ use $K(t,f)^2=\inf_{f=f_0+f_1}(\|f_0\|_{E_0}^2+t^2\|f_1\|_{E_1}^2)$. In the spectral $L^2,H^1$ pair, independent minimization of each coefficient gives $K(t,f)^2=\sum_j|f_j|^2t^2w_j/(1+t^2w_j)$. Integration against $t^{-2}\,dt$ yields a fixed positive multiple of $\sum_jw_j^{1/2}|f_j|^2$, by substituting $t\sqrt{w_j}$ and Tonelli. Use the single-boundary versions of the chart maps: $Gf=((\psi_jf)\circ\phi_j^{-1})_j$ and $L(v)=\sum_j\psi_j(v_j\circ\phi_j)$, with zero extension. The finite chart Jacobian bounds and product rule give their $L^2,H^1$ bounds, while $\sum_j\psi_j^2=1$ gives $LG=I$, exactly as in [F3] with one chart factor. These maps bound the respective $K$ functionals in both directions (apply either map to every decomposition, using its endpoint bounds and its left inverse). For a compactly supported chart function the identical Fourier calculation gives weight $(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$. This is equivalent to its Slobodeckij norm: Parseval applied to $f(\cdot+h)-f$ and integration against $|h|^{-n-1}\,dh$ give the homogeneous weight $c_n|\xi|$, with $0<c_n<\infty$ by splitting $|h|\le1$ and $|h|>1$. Thus [F2] identifies the trace quotient with $H^{1/2}_\Delta/\mathbb R$, and duality identifies its mean-zero dual with $H^{-1/2}_\Delta$. The counting estimate [F1] implies $w_j^{-1/2}\le C(1+j)^{-1/n}$, after enlarging the constant for finitely many low modes. By [F5], $R=\mathscr R_\gamma$ maps the $L^2$ unit ball into a uniformly bounded $H^1_\Delta$ ball. If $P_J$ is the first $J$-mode projection, then $R_J=P_JR$ has rank at most $J$ and $\|R-R_J\|\le C(1+J)^{-1/n}$. Likewise $S=C_M^{r/2}$ has the rank-$J$ approximation $S_J=P_JS$ with $\|S-S_J\|\le C(1+J)^{-r/n}$; for $r=0$ this means the bound one and does not assert that $S$ is compact. [A1, F1, F2, F5, given, construct]

Put $B=\mathscr R_\gamma-\mathscr R_{\gamma_0}$ and $s=\|\kappa_\gamma-\kappa_{\gamma_0}\|_2$. By [F4], $s^2=\sum_{i,j}|b_{ij}|^2w_j^{-r}$. Choose $L$ so large that both $\sum_iw_i^{1-2L}$ and $\sum_jw_j^{r+1-2L}$ converge by [F1]. Then [F5] gives $T:=\sum_{i,j}|b_{ij}|^2w_iw_j^{r+1}\le C$, uniformly over every conductivity pair. Cauchy–Schwarz now yields $\sum_{i,j}w_i^{1/2}w_j^{1/2}|b_{ij}|^2\le (\sum|b_{ij}|^2w_j^{-r})^{1/2}(\sum|b_{ij}|^2w_iw_j^{r+1})^{1/2}\le C s$. The left side is the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm from $H^{-1/2}_\Delta$ to $H^{1/2}_\Delta$: the normalized input basis is $w_j^{1/4}e_j$. Taking square roots and [F5]'s quotient norm equivalence gives $\|B\|_{\mathcal L(\dot{\mathcal D}^*,\dot{\mathcal D})}\le C s^{1/2}$, also when $s=0$. [F1, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

For clarity, the inverse assertion in [F6] uses no boundary pointwise differentiability: the Dirichlet weak solution with boundary class $g$ has Neumann functional $\dot\Lambda_\gamma g$, and uniqueness of the weak Neumann problem gives $\mathscr R_\gamma\dot\Lambda_\gamma g=g$; conversely the weak Neumann solution satisfies its own Dirichlet problem, giving $\dot\Lambda_\gamma\mathscr R_\gamma F=F$. Therefore $\dot\Lambda_\gamma-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_0}=\dot\Lambda_\gamma(\mathscr R_{\gamma_0}-\mathscr R_\gamma)\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_0}$. Uniform DN operator bounds in [F6] and step 3.1 prove the displayed square-root comparison. Together with step 2.1 this establishes all assertions. [F6, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

The compact operator $RS$ therefore has singular values $s_j\le C(1+j)^{-(1+r)/n}$. Apply [F3] to obtain the unique $L^2$ kernel and norm equality. Input and output annihilation of the constant mode mean that its integral in either variable is zero, by testing the integral operator and its adjoint on the constant function. First apply the finite Fourier multiplier $P_N$ from step 2.1, retaining the WHOLE real Fourier polynomial, including both sine and cosine components of each nonzero frequency. Its coefficient vectors lie in a compact set, so all its pointwise values are uniformly bounded. Inject the finitely many retained real basis functions $\varphi_j(x)$ as periodic bias channels. The multiplication map $(z,t)\mapsto zt$ is continuous on the compact ranges of $(P_Nf)(x)$ and $\varphi_j(x)$; approximate it by the pointwise networks of [F2], then use a zero-frequency multiplier to average each product.
